standard.title: Plan and refine investigations
standard.description: Plan and conduct statistical investigations by posing and refining questions or identifying a problem and collecting relevant data; analyse and interpret the data and communicate findings within the context of the investigation
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can plan and conduct statistical investigations, choose appropriate displays and communicate findings (AC9M5ST03). They have experience with the full investigation cycle. They have not yet practised refining questions based on initial findings or working with the full range of variable types from AC9M6ST01.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students can plan and conduct statistical investigations by posing and refining questions, collecting relevant data, analysing and interpreting results, and communicating findings in context.

nodes.label: Posing and refining the investigation question
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can pose a statistical question for investigation, identify what data is needed, and refine the question based on feasibility or initial findings.
nodes.minimum_width: Pose a statistical question; identify what data would answer it; consider whether the data is collectible; refine the question if needed to make it answerable.
nodes.typical_width: Pose questions that lead to interesting statistical investigations; distinguish statistical questions (expecting variability) from mathematical questions (single answer); anticipate potential issues with data collection before starting; refine based on a pilot sample.
wider: Investigate question design — how does the wording of a question affect what data is collected? Compare two different phrasings of the same question.
Pose a question from a real community context and discuss how the question framing affects who would want to investigate it

response_modes.reason: Students who generate only one investigation question type (e.g. 'how many...') develop a narrow concept of statistical investigation. Exposure to comparison questions, association questions, and change-over-time questions broadens the concept of what statistical investigation can address.

success_criteria: Student poses a statistical question and explains what data is needed to answer it.
Student identifies at least one way the question could be refined for better investigation.

nodes.label: Collecting and organising relevant data
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can select and use data collection methods appropriate to their investigation question, collect data systematically, and organise it for analysis.
nodes.minimum_width: Design a simple data collection method for a given investigation question; collect data from at least 20 observations; organise in a table or frequency display.
nodes.typical_width: Design appropriate collection instruments (survey, observation tally, measurement record); consider sample selection; collect and organise data for analysis including categorical and numerical variables; check data for recording errors.
wider: Investigate secondary data sources — existing datasets from government, sport, or census sources — and discuss how they differ from primary collection
Consider ethical data collection: what questions are appropriate to ask? How should data about people be stored and shared?

response_modes.reason: Systematic data collection and organisation are procedural skills requiring care and precision. Errors in recording or organisation propagate through the entire investigation. This is a genuine consolidation point — accuracy here is the prerequisite for meaningful analysis.

nodes.hinge_reason: Errors or gaps in data collection and organisation propagate directly into Node 3 — analysis and interpretation can only be as reliable as the dataset permits. Students with poorly organised or incomplete data cannot draw valid conclusions regardless of analytical skill.
success_criteria: Student collects data using a method appropriate to the investigation question.
Student organises the data in a form that supports analysis.

nodes.label: Analysing, interpreting and communicating findings
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can analyse collected data using appropriate measures and displays, interpret the findings in context, and communicate conclusions that address the original investigation question.
nodes.minimum_width: Calculate mode and range from collected data; create an appropriate display; state at least two findings that address the investigation question in context.
nodes.typical_width: Analyse data using mode, range, shape, and appropriate displays; interpret findings in context; connect findings back to the original question; acknowledge limitations of the investigation (sample size, bias, data quality); communicate as a written or presented report.
wider: Refine the investigation based on findings — pose a follow-up question that the initial investigation raised and plan how it could be addressed
Communicate findings to a real or simulated audience (class, school community, partner class) and respond to questions about methods and conclusions

response_modes.reason: Communicating findings integrates data analysis, contextual interpretation, and critical reflection on the investigation's limitations. The coordination of these — producing a coherent response to the original question — is the defining capability goal of this descriptor.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Statistical investigations are open-ended and the quality of findings scales with the sophistication of analysis and communication. Advancing students who refine questions and communicate to authentic audiences engage at a meaningfully higher level without exceeding the year band.
success_criteria: Student produces an appropriate display and states findings using statistical measures.
Student communicates conclusions that specifically address the original investigation question.
